approval.cost: No fee for registering an app or requesting Graph permissions is stated in the docs read; no price appears for publisher verification or Microsoft 365 Certification either
approval.trigger: No Microsoft app review or approval is required for an app registration to go live: no app-store-style review, no pre-approval user/install cap, no stated fee. The real gate is consent, and it is per-tenant, not global. Per the OneDrive permissions reference, all delegated Files.* permissions show 'Admin Consent Required: No', so an individual user can consent for their own files (by contrast, all application Files.* permissions and delegated Sites.FullControl.All require admin consent, and 'only an administrator... can consent to application permissions'). However, each work/school tenant controls user consent via User consent settings: admins can allow user consent for all apps, allow it only 'for apps from verified publishers, for selected permissions', or disallow user consent entirely. If a user cannot consent, they hit an 'admin approval required' error and (if enabled) the admin consent workflow, where designated reviewers approve or deny. Consequence: the same app can be self-serve in one customer tenant and admin-gated in another, and an unverified publisher's app may be un-consentable by end users in tenants using Microsoft's recommended setting even though the Files.* permissions themselves don't require admin consent. Publisher verification is therefore the practical 'approval' to obtain: 'App publishers verify their identity with Microsoft by associating their app registration with their verified Microsoft Partner Network (MPN) account... After you become a verified publisher, a blue verified badge displays in your app's Microsoft Entra consent prompts.' It is not mandatory. Optional: the consent prompt can also display a Microsoft 365 Certification logo ('an app is vetted against controls derived from leading industry standard frameworks'); certification is not required for users to connect.
approval.wait: No review applies; publisher verification has no stated duration

blockers.detail: Registering as work/school-only locks out all personal OneDrive users, and vice versa. The app object also 'can't be moved between different tenants' after creation.
blockers.howToClear: Choose 'Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts' at registration if consumer OneDrive matters.
blockers.title: Account-type choice is the OneDrive trap

blockers.detail: Users can self-consent to Files.* delegated permissions, but a tenant with restrictive user-consent settings (or an app requesting any admin-restricted permission, e.g. Sites.FullControl.All) forces the admin consent workflow: an out-of-band human approval you cannot automate or expedite.
blockers.howToClear: Become a verified publisher, keep permissions to the user-consentable Files.* set, and prepare an admin-consent guide for customer IT.
blockers.title: Admin-consent asymmetry across tenants

blockers.detail: SPA-platform refresh tokens die after 24 hours while server-side web apps get the 90-day rolling window. Refresh tokens are also revoked on events like password changes, so reconnection UX is mandatory.
blockers.howToClear: Register the app as a Web platform for server-side flows and build a re-connect path.
blockers.title: Refresh-token platform split

alternatives: App-only (application permissions + client credentials flow): Files.Read.All / Files.ReadWrite.All application permissions read/write files in all site collections with no signed-in user; admin consent is mandatory; suited to tenant-wide migration/backup daemons, not 'users connect their own account'
App-folder flavor: Files.ReadWrite.AppFolder restricts the app to its own app root folder in the user's OneDrive (personal accounts only); least-privilege for apps that only store their own data

File-picker flavor: Files.Read.Selected / Files.ReadWrite.Selected (preview, work/school only, for Office file handlers); the user picks individual files and 'The app has access for several hours after the user selects a file'
flavor.recommended: One multitenant Microsoft Entra ID app registration using the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (with PKCE), requesting Microsoft Graph delegated Files.* permissions plus offline_access
flavor.why: There is no OneDrive-specific app object. The object is a Microsoft Entra ID 'app registration' (Microsoft identity platform), identified by an Application (client) ID. 'OneDrive' access is Microsoft Graph drive/file access (/me/drive, driveItem resources) granted through Graph delegated permissions in the Files.* family. The key OneDrive-specific decision is Supported account types: OneDrive exists in two worlds (personal OneDrive on consumer Microsoft accounts, and OneDrive for Business on work/school Entra ID accounts), and only 'Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts' accepts both; you must also call the common (or consumers) authority endpoint or consumer users cannot sign in at all. A generic M365/Entra app is usually single-tenant or work/school-only. Permission validity differs by account type: Files.Read, Files.ReadWrite, Files.Read.All, and Files.ReadWrite.All delegated permissions 'are valid on both personal Microsoft accounts and work or school accounts'; Files.ReadWrite.AppFolder is only valid for personal accounts; Sites.* permissions (SharePoint, which backs OneDrive for Business) are only valid on work or school accounts. For personal accounts, Files.Read/Files.ReadWrite also cover files shared with the user.

humanMust: Register the app in the Microsoft Entra admin center (App registrations > New registration) and set Supported account types to include personal Microsoft accounts
Add a platform and redirect URI(s) (e.g. Web platform with your HTTPS callback)
Create a client secret (or upload a certificate) under Certificates & secrets
Configure API permissions (Microsoft Graph delegated: Files.Read/Files.ReadWrite, offline_access; User.Read is assigned by default)
(Recommended) Become a verified publisher by associating the app registration with a verified Microsoft Partner Network (MPN) account
name: OneDrive
nuances: Delegated = user-bounded: 'The application is only able to read files that the user can personally access'; delegated tokens never exceed the connecting user's own file permissions, and SharePoint/OneDrive performs its own per-file authorization check on every call. Inside each customer tenant, a service principal for your app is created automatically on first consent; tenant admins may optionally pre-grant tenant-wide admin consent.

Static vs dynamic consent can't be mixed: requesting https://graph.microsoft.com/.default together with individual scopes in one request errors; .default means 'all permissions configured on the app registration'.

offline_access is implicit but must be explicit: although 'if any delegated permission is granted, offline_access is implicitly granted' for consent purposes, on the v2.0 endpoint 'your app must explicitly request the offline_access scope, to receive refresh tokens'. Refresh-token behavior: 'Refresh tokens replace themselves with a fresh token upon every use. The Microsoft identity platform doesn't revoke old refresh tokens when used to fetch new access tokens.'

Token figures (provider-stated): access token 'valid for around one hour' (default lifetime 'a random value ranging between 60-90 minutes (75 minutes on average)'; with CAE-capable client/resource it 'may be automatically extended to 24-28 hours'); authorization codes 'typically expire after about 10 minutes'; ID token about 1 hour.
prerequisites: A Microsoft account / Entra tenant to host the app registration
The account-types decision (personal + work/school) made at registration
A verified MPN account if pursuing verified-publisher status

steps.detail: Microsoft Entra admin center > App registrations > New registration: set the name and Supported account types ('Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts' for OneDrive). 'Once created, the application object can't be moved between different tenants.'
steps.title: Register the app (multitenant incl. personal accounts)

steps.detail: Add a platform and redirect URI(s) (e.g. Web platform with your HTTPS callback). Create a client secret (or upload a certificate) under Certificates & secrets. Configure API permissions: Microsoft Graph delegated User.Read (default), Files.Read or Files.ReadWrite, and offline_access (portal configuration, or request scopes dynamically at sign-in).
steps.title: Platform, secret, and Graph permissions

steps.detail: Associate the app registration with a verified Microsoft Partner Network (MPN) account; a blue 'verified' badge then appears on consent prompts. Tenants that restrict user consent to verified publishers will otherwise block end users from consenting.
steps.title: (Recommended) Become a verified publisher

steps.detail: Redirect to login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize with response_type=code, scope, and PKCE parameters. The user signs in and consents on Microsoft's page (or is diverted into their tenant's admin consent workflow).
steps.title: Send the user to authorize (common authority)

steps.detail: Exchange the authorization code (lifetime about 10 minutes) at the /oauth2/v2.0/token endpoint for access + refresh tokens; store the refresh token per user (and per tenant ID for work accounts). Call Microsoft Graph (GET /me/drive/...) with the access token; silently refresh before the roughly 1-hour expiry.
steps.title: Exchange the code; call Graph; refresh

tagline: There is no OneDrive app: it is a Microsoft Entra ID app registration asking for Microsoft Graph Files permissions, and the real approval lives inside each customer tenant's consent settings, not with Microsoft. Get the account-types choice wrong and half of OneDrive's users cannot sign in at all.

time.active: ~15 min of portal setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day for self-consent tenants; admin-gated tenants depend on their reviewers
time.waiting: None from Microsoft; per-tenant admin consent workflow durations are tenant-controlled
